notes: Corruption: a dark mirror to trust. What you do in the dark changes what you are — and people can feel it, even when they can't name it.
You can butcher the dead for meat now — and eat it. The first time will haunt you. It gets easier. That's the horror.
In a healthy village, discovered cannibalism means exile. In a starving or corrupted one, the rules change — and fear becomes its own currency.
Rare dark pasts: sometimes you wake as one of the village's hidden dark ones, with a history that explains it.
Villagers fight with better judgment: they commit to fights they can win, call for help when outmatched, and only flee when it's truly hopeless.
The fallen keep their real belongings on the body — open the pack to take, leave, or use. Keepsakes are buried with their owner.
Crafting menu now shows every recipe you've seen, with honest odds. Villagers fetch their own armor and use the pharmacy before a healer.
The Craft screen now lists recipes you're learning — early attempts are honest blind tries (materials stay hidden until you've learned them).
Map monster popups no longer name creatures the village hasn't named yet.
Gristlefit rage can lash out at allies mid-fight — and now they remember it. Trust drops, and it haunts you.
Trying to strike an ally in a fight gets an honest refusal instead of silence.
Boiling water now honestly costs time and energy — bulk purification was free on the action clock.
Storms wrecking your camp wake you with a start — no more sleeping through the destruction in tent-quality comfort.
Rain and storm water now respect your carry limit.
Fixed the pantry quietly generating ~1,000 free calories a day.
The dead no longer eat: fallen villagers stop consuming and producing food.
Food sharing and meal draws are now honestly tracked.
Your gear is yours: villagers keep their own belongings. The village stash only holds what someone deliberately deposits.
New armory (weapons) and pharmacy (medicine) sections in the village stash.
The dead carry their real belongings — open their packs and loot.
13 craftable weapons and armor (spears, bows, bark armor, hide armor…) through the normal crafting menu.
Closed trust-farming exploits around interpreter gestures and food gifts.
Settled promises no longer block you from making new ones.
Fixed villagers fighting unarmed — they now actually equip the weapons they carry.
Villagers gear up and get patched up by the healer before heading into danger.
Closed mid-fight examine and interact exploits.
Combat honesty pass: war cries, threats, and calls for help now say what they mean.
Fixed betrayal fights breaking across save/load.
Fixed pemmican showing the wrong calories.
